The latch / catch mechanism that locks the pump spring in the cocked position is worn down, or misaligned, so it is slipping - I had a pellet gun that did that. We took it apart, filed the latch back just a bit to a sharper edge - oiled up the pump seal, and it was better than new after that. No more misfires. Filed both sides of the front sight to a finer point while we were at it. Easier to see the target.

Kick ass pellet weapon of squirrel death. The improved pump gives the pellet more speed / power too = overall better accuracy.

So, Crosman makes a bunch of 13xx models, probably all very similar under the hood.

Looking at the parts diagram for the 1377c - the part # 22 Sear - and maybe part # 25 - the Sear spring, that is probably the source of the problem. Looking above that you have a compression spring #15, and a striker #17. So it looks like the sear locks the striker in the loaded position compressing spring #15. The Sear #22 looks to be a perfect fit for the striker.

Either the Sear is worn or misaligned so the fit is no longer perfect, or perhaps the Sear spring #25 is worn or misaligned so as not to be pushing the Sear all the way up for a tight fit when you re-cock it. When that slips it is causing the misfires.

Now I may have this wrong, or your model may be slightly different, but the principle of the thing is the same. You need a tight fit to hold that compression spring in place until you pull the trigger.
